text:
A: Hello! Can you hear me alright, mate?
B: Yeah, I can hear you. Darren.
A: Darren, nice one, I'm Daniel. Whereabouts are you, Darren?
B: Bridgwater. Somerset.
A: Oh, lovely. Somerset. Cider country, innit? Sorry, that's probably the first thing everyone says.
B: Pretty much, yeah. Not wrong, mind.
A: Ha. I'm in Walthamstow, east London. I teach, Head of History at a big academy. What do you do yourself?
B: Cleaning. Part-time, at a supermarket. Early mornings.
A: How early are we talking?
B: Up at half four.
A: Half four! Mate, that's brutal. I thought I had it bad with the Victoria line this morning, it was absolutely rammed. Honestly, you remind me of my dad a bit. He was an electrician, self-employed, out the door at six every day of his life. Never complained once. Well, he complained a bit.
B: Ha. Sounds about right. Where's he to, then, your dad?
A: Chelmsford, where I grew up. He's had some heart trouble recently, actually, so I'm trying to get back more. Not doing very well at it, if I'm honest.
B: Sorry to hear that. It's hard when they get older. Mine went about eight years back.
A: Ah, I'm sorry, mate. That's... yeah.
B: You're alright. Go and see him, though, while you can. That's all I'd say.
A: No, you're right. You're right. I keep saying I will. Er, anyway, did you do the puzzle bit at the start? I sort of flew through it, but that's the pub quiz brain, I captain our team.
B: Got about half. Not my thing. I do darts on a Thursday, that's about as brainy as I get.
A: Darts is maths, though! Proper mental arithmetic. You could teach my Year 9s a thing or two, do you know what I mean?
B: Er, I dunno about that. I'm rubbish. It's mostly for the pint.
A: Ha, that's the real reason for any team, innit. I play five-a-side Wednesdays and I'm convinced it's just an excuse for the pub after. I did the Hackney Half last year as well, which nearly killed me, but I got a decent time.
B: Fair play. My knee'd go before I got to the end of the road.
A: Who are you with, football-wise?
B: Bristol City.
A: Oh, nice, proper club. I'm West Ham, which, after Saturday, I'd rather not talk about.
B: Ha. Join the club, mate. We was terrible an' all.
A: Misery loves company. So what do you do for fun down there, apart from darts? Is it all cider farms and—
